source_text:
Epistula ad Photium presbyterum
Τοῦ αὐτοῦ πρὸς Φώτιον πρεσβύτερονἈλεξανδρείας·
Εἰ δὲ κέκρανται αἱ δύο φύσεις εἰς μῖξιν μίαν, ἑτεροούσιοι τυγχάνουσαι, οὐδ'
ὁποτέρα σώζεται, ἀλλ' ἀμφότεραι συγχυθεῖσαι ἠφανίσθησαν.
orientation: Cyril is stating the logical consequence of a hypothetical position in his letter to Photius.
pass_a_gloss: But if the two natures have been blended into one mixture, being of different substance, neither one is preserved, but both, having been confused, were destroyed.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'of different substance' for ἑτεροούσιοι, and τυγχάνουσαι is rendered as a circumstantial participle 'being' to preserve the participial force.
rejected: since they are of different substance

choices.why: οὐδ' ὁποτέρα is an emphatic negative meaning 'not either one'; 'neither one' preserves the singular distributive force.
rejected: no one of them is preserved

choices.why: The aorist passive participle συγχυθεῖσαι is rendered as 'having been confused' to keep the participle distinct from the main verb, and ἠφανίσθησαν as 'were destroyed' per the glossary.

pass_b_english: If two natures of different substance have been blended into one mixture, neither one is preserved; instead, both are confused and destroyed.
